deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is a bifolium sheet with two short non-mathematical texts.

(1) Left half: a draft or copy of a short formal cover letter, with corrections. It is addressed to an official ('Ew. Wohlgeboren'), presumably the treasurer (Rendant) of the Göttingen Professoren-Witwen-(und Waisen-)Kasse, the professors' widows' fund. Reading of the main text: 'Ew. Wohlgeboren erlaube ich mir meinen Beitrag zur Professoren-Witwen-Kasse für den Zeitraum vom 1. Oct. 1861/62 mit 15 [Thlr? / currency abbreviation unclear] Gold gehorsamst zu übersenden und bitte [um gefällige Angabe / die Quittung] dem Überbringer zu geben. Hochachtungsvoll Ew. Wohlgeboren gehorsamst [unsigned].' Several phrases are struck through or replaced: 'um gefällige', 'gefälligst', 'dem', 'zu geben'. The letter transmits the annual contribution for the year starting 1 October 1861 (financial year 1861/62). Riemann had been ordinary professor since 1859, which would make him liable to contribute. He married Elise Koch in June 1862, so the widows' fund was directly relevant to him at this time.

(2) Right half: a household laundry or linen list headed '[d.? / 18]63 Juni'. It reads: 6 Mannshemden (men's shirts), 3 Frauenhemden (women's shirts), 1 Unterrock (petticoat). It is signed '[?]. Riemann'. Given the women's garments and the date of June 1863, after the marriage, the hand and signature may be Elise Riemann's ('E. Riemann') rather than Bernhard's. The initial is uncertain. The isolated '1' at the right margin is the archival folio number.

There is no derivation to reconstruct. The next page has Riemann-surface style drawings (closed curves around branch points joined by cuts) and a fragment of the integral of dz/(z-1). This shows the sheet was later reused as scrap paper for mathematics.

results.what: Draft cover letter remitting the annual contribution to the Göttingen professors' widows' fund for 1861/62, plus a household linen list dated June 1863

deep.surprise_reason: The page is purely administrative and domestic: a widows'-fund payment letter and a laundry list. It has minor biographical interest, documenting Riemann's professorial obligations around 1861/62 and his household after his 1862 marriage, but no mathematical content.

checkable.asserts: Total number of garments on the linen list (trivial; there is no mathematical content to verify)

transcription_corrections: 'rf' before 'Gold' is an unclear currency abbreviation. It is most plausibly a Thaler abbreviation ('Thlr'/'rh'), i.e. 15 Thaler in gold, but this is uncertain.
The header of the right column ('f 63 Juni') is more likely '[18]63 Juni' or 'd. 13 Juni'. The first symbol is unclear.
The signature initial read as 'B.' is uncertain. It may be 'E.' (Elise Riemann), consistent with the household content and the June 1863 date.

The interlinear insertion above the struck-through 'um gefällige' reads roughly 'um gefällige Angabe' (uncertain). 'dem' before 'Überbringer' and 'zu geben' are struck through, as is 'gefälligst' after 'Quittung'.
'Professoren-Witwen-Kasse': the image reads 'Professoren-Witwen-' at the line end followed by 'Kasse' (spelled 'Casse' or 'Kasse').
The lone '1' in the right margin is a folio number, not part of the text.
